setting: A fictional 20-minute team meeting, chaired by the learner, about a decision the learner has made.

presentation.situation: You manage a software team. You decided to move the weekly release from Friday to Tuesday, starting {{start}}. Alex and Maya have concerns. Chair the meeting: set the purpose, hear each person, and end with who does what by when.
presentation.opening: Before we accept this move to Tuesday releases, the two of us have concerns. How do you want to run this?

brief.you_are: You are the team manager and you are chairing this 20-minute meeting.
brief.situation: You decided to move the weekly release from Friday to Tuesday, starting {{start}}, because {{reason}}. Alex (operations lead) and Maya (testing lead) have concerns. You may delay the start by up to two weeks and you may lend Maya one person from another team.
brief.task: Say what the meeting is for, make sure Alex and Maya each get heard one at a time, then finish by naming who will do what and by when.
brief.done_looks_like: Both concerns are out in the open, you have made a decision, and each action has an owner and a date.

participants.name: You
participants.authority: Final decision on the release plan
goals: Chair the meeting and close with owners and dates

participants.name: Alex
participants.relationship: Reports to you; runs the on-call rota

card.want: Enough notice to redo the on-call rota fairly before any change starts.
card.hidden_need: Was not consulted and feels the team's personal plans were ignored.
card.attitude: Direct, experienced and a little irritated, but reasonable once given a real date.
card.speech: Plain, confident workplace English. Short sentences. Uses concrete details, not slogans.
tactics: Talk over Maya if nobody manages the discussion
Ask 'so what have we actually decided?' if the chair drifts

pressure.gentle: Raises the concern once and listens.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Questions why the decision was made without the team, firmly and without insults.

participants.name: Maya
participants.relationship: Reports to you; leads release testing

card.want: Enough testing capacity for a Monday regression run before a Tuesday release.
card.hidden_need: Worried that she will be blamed if a rushed release fails.
card.attitude: Careful and evidence-minded. Quieter than Alex, but firm about risk.
card.speech: Clear, precise English. States numbers from what she knows and says when something is unknown.
tactics: Wait to be asked unless the beat brings her in
Ask who is accountable if testing is cut short

pressure.balanced: Asks how the capacity gap will be covered.
pressure.challenging: Will not agree to a date until the capacity gap has an owner.

ledger.text: The decision is to move the weekly release from Friday to Tuesday, starting {{start}}.
The meeting is booked for 20 minutes.
{{rota}} engineers would have to change their on-call week because of the move.
Alex needs two weeks' notice to redo the on-call rota fairly.
A Tuesday release needs a full regression test on Monday, which takes one full day.
Maya has {{testers}} testers and one of them is on leave until {{leave}}.
The cost of any extra testing is not known.

objectives.description: Set a clear purpose for the meeting
objectives.evidence: The learner states what the meeting is for or how it will run, in their own words.
alternatives: We're here to hear your concerns and agree a plan for the move

objectives.evidence: The learner actively directs the discussion so each person is heard: inviting someone, stopping an interruption, or summarising before moving on.
alternatives: Maya, hold on, let me hear Alex first, then you

objectives.evidence: The learner states a decision and at least one named owner with an action and a time.
alternatives: Alex will redo the rota by Friday; Maya gets one extra person from next week

examples: The purpose of this meeting is ...
Alex, let's hear you first, then Maya.
To close: Alex will ... by ...; Maya will ... by ...
prerequisites: Read the decision and your options in the briefing.

beats.goal: The chair must set the purpose. Until they do, Alex presses them for it.
signals: \b(?:purpose|agenda|we(?:'re| are) here|goal of|today we|first we|the point of|meeting is|i want to hear|let'?s start)\b
opportunity: Before anything else, what exactly do you want from this meeting?
We have 20 minutes. What are we here to decide?
beats.orient: You're the chair, and you decided to move the release from Friday to Tuesday. Maya and I have concerns. Tell us what this meeting is for and who should speak first.
fallback: We have 20 minutes. What do you want to get out of this?
I just need to know what we're deciding today.

beats.goal: Alex and Maya each have a real concern and compete for time. The chair must manage them.
signals: \b(?:let me hear|one at a time|hold on|go ahead|go first|your turn|what do you think|alex,|maya,|let'?s hear|so you(?:'re| are)|if i understand)\b
beats.second_line: Sorry to cut in, but the testing problem is just as serious, and nobody has asked me yet.
opportunity: {{rota}} engineers would have to change their on-call week. I need two weeks to redo the rota fairly.
Can one of us finish a point? Who do you want to hear from?
beats.orient: You're running this meeting, so you decide who talks. You can say: Alex, go first, and then Maya. We each have one concern for you to hear.
fallback: The on-call rota is my concern. I need notice to change it fairly.
Whose concern do you want to deal with first?

beats.goal: Time is nearly up. The team needs a decision with owners and dates.
opportunity: We're nearly out of time. So what have we actually decided?
Who is doing what, and by when?
beats.orient: The meeting is almost over. As chair, say what you've decided, then give each of us one action and a date. You can delay the start by up to two weeks and lend me one person.
fallback: I need to know who is doing what, and by when.
Please give us a decision before we finish.

closing_line: Good, that's clear. We'll get on with those actions.

o1.good: One sentence saying why everyone is here and what will come out of it, before the discussion starts.
common_mistakes: Reacting to the first objection instead of framing the meeting
Asking 'what are the concerns?' with no purpose
o1.micro_lesson: Chairs speak first about the purpose. It gives you the right to steer later.
o1.model: We're here to hear your concerns about the move and leave with a plan that works.
o1.smaller_step: Finish this sentence: The purpose of this meeting is ...

o2.good: Deciding who speaks, protecting the quieter person, and summarising one point before moving on.
common_mistakes: Letting the louder person keep talking
Answering every point yourself instead of hearing both
o2.micro_lesson: You own the floor. Name the next speaker and the order, and summarise before you switch.
o2.model: Alex, finish your point. Maya, you're next. So far I've heard the rota needs two weeks' notice.
o2.smaller_step: Name who should talk next, and who comes after them.

o3.good: A clear decision, then each action with one owner and one date.
common_mistakes: Listing actions with no owner or date
o3.micro_lesson: An action is not finished until it has a name and a date.
o3.model: We'll start two weeks later. Alex redoes the rota by next Friday; Maya gets one extra tester from Monday.
o3.smaller_step: Give one person one action and one date.

variants.start: the first week of next month
variants.reason: three of the last twelve Friday releases failed and left customers with no weekend support
two Friday releases caused weekend outages this quarter and support staff had to work overtime
